shorts.title: Trump On Ambassador Guilfoyle: "We're Not Happy" #Shorts
shorts.narration: [serious] Folks, President Trump just said three words about his own ambassador that nobody in Athens wants to hear. [beat] "We're not happy." [serious] On Monday, asked about Kimberly Guilfoyle, ambassador to Greece, Trump told reporters, "We're looking at it." The Wall Street Journal has reported allegations that she threatened a host-country official and offered administration influence in return for a credit card bill being paid. Her lawyers deny wrongdoing and say the money was payment for unpaid services. [sarcastic] Democrats Gregory Meeks, Jeanne Shaheen and Robert Garcia now want an investigation. [beat] Democrats discovering ethics. A Monday miracle. [warm] Proverbs 22:1 says, "A good name is rather to be chosen than great riches." [beat] And a credit card bill in the headlines is nobody's good name. [mischievously] So, Democrats: would you fire one of your own that fast? Tell me below, and subscribe, because Henry roasts the news every day.

claims.text: Trump said Monday, Oct. 12, 2026 that he is "looking at" firing Ambassador to Greece Kimberly Guilfoyle; to reporters at the White House he said: "Well, we're looking at it." and "We're not happy."
Trump said "We're looking at it" and "We're not happy." about Guilfoyle on Monday, Oct. 12, 2026.

The Wall Street Journal has alleged a threat to a host-country official, improper gifts and services, and an offer to use administration influence in return for payment of a credit card bill; the article presents these as allegations.
Guilfoyle's lawyers deny wrongdoing and say the money she sought from a Trump donor was payment for unpaid services.
Democratic lawmakers Gregory Meeks, Jeanne Shaheen and Robert Garcia have called for an investigation.

shorts.title: Mamdani Vowed To Disband The SRG. Nine Months Later: A 'Review' #Shorts
shorts.narration: [amused] Folks, New York Mayor Zohran Mamdani promised to disband the NYPD's Strategic Response Group. [beat] Nine months later, it's still there, and he just launched a review. [serious] On Monday, Mamdani announced a sweeping review of NYPD use-of-force policies. Fox News reports that, more than nine months into his term, he hasn't disbanded the unit, eliminated its database of suspected gang members, or stopped arrests for low-level offenses. He's also kept Jessica Tisch, the commissioner Eric Adams appointed. [sarcastic] On X, he once wrote, "As Mayor, I will disband the SRG." [beat] Turns out, as Mayor, he will form a review. [warm] Matthew 5:37 says, "let your communication be, Yea, yea; Nay, nay." [beat] Mamdani's version: yea, yea, pending review. [mischievously] So, Democrats: is a promise just a campaign poster with an expiration date? Fight me in the comments, and subscribe, because Henry roasts the news every day.

claims.text: On Monday, Oct. 12, 2026, NYC Mayor Zohran Mamdani launched an internal review of NYPD use-of-force policies.

More than nine months into his term, Mamdani has not disbanded the Strategic Response Group (SRG), eliminated its database of suspected gang members, or stopped arresting people for low-level offenses, per Fox News.
Mamdani kept Police Commissioner Jessica Tisch, whom former Mayor Eric Adams appointed.
Mamdani wrote on X after announcing his mayoral bid: "As Mayor, I will disband the SRG, which has cost taxpayers millions in lawsuit settlements".

shorts.title: Judge Erupts At DOJ Over Trump's Golf Course Trees: 'Lost Credibility' #Shorts
shorts.hook: Judge vs. DOJ over golf course trees
shorts.narration: [incredulous] Folks, a federal judge just went off on the Justice Department over trees. [beat] Golf course trees. [serious] On Monday, Judge Ana Reyes, a Biden appointee, held an emergency hearing on tree removal at East Potomac Golf Links in Washington, where Trump wants a championship-caliber course. A government lawyer acknowledged about 430 trees were already cut. Fox News reports that journalist Scott MacFarlane's live-tweets had Reyes telling the government, "You've lost credibility!" The administration says the cutting follows a 2019 Park Service plan, separate from Trump's redesign. [serious] Former Obama ethics lawyer Norm Eisen's group cheered the hearing. [beat] Friends, the resistance has found its final frontier: a par four. [warm] Psalm 1:3 says the righteous is "like a tree planted by the rivers of water." [beat] These trees never got a vote. [mischievously] So, is this a court fight or a tee time? Comments below, and subscribe, because Henry roasts the news every day.

claims.text: On Monday, Oct. 12, 2026, Judge Ana Reyes, a Biden appointee, held an emergency hearing on removal of hundreds of trees at East Potomac Golf Links (Hains Point), Washington, D.C., challenged by preservationists.
Trump wants to turn the historic course into a championship-caliber layout.
A government lawyer acknowledged about 430 trees had already been cut.
Per journalist Scott MacFarlane's live-tweets as cited by Fox News, Reyes said: "You've lost credibility!"
The administration says the removals implement a 2019 National Park Service landscape-restoration plan and are separate from Trump's proposed course redesign.
Former Obama ethics lawyer Norm Eisen, through the Democracy Defenders Fund, publicly celebrated the court agreeing to hear the case on an emergency basis.
